newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends up, led by Lujiazui.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends up, led by Lujiazui.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up on Monday, with some domestic investors buying Pudong shares, especially Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co Ltd, brokers said.
But they said most overseas institutions remained on the sidelines, waiting for the release of the bulk of the 1996 company reports, due by April 30.
The index rose 0.554 points or 0.81 percent to 69.099 points on volume of 22.7 million shares worth $9.6 million.
Brokers said strong performance of Pudong shares on the A share market increased domestic buying in Pudong shares on the B share market in the afternoon session.
"Domestic investors' confidence in the B share market is supporting the market steadily," one broker said.
Another broker said the market was still in a consolidation mode and the index would linger around the 69-point in the short term.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, with 23 up, seven flat and 12 down.

Real estate developer Shanghai Wai Gaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development, the most active counter, was the star on a technical rebound, up $0.024 or 5.55 percent to $0.456 on volume of 2.7 million shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development, another Pudong real estate company, was the third winner, gaining $0.032 or 3.77 percent to $0.880 on volume of 1.9 million shares.
Shanghai's A shares ended up on gains amongst Pudong shares, with continued inflow of fresh capital, brokers said.
The index rose 23.350 points or 2.07 percent to 1,150.391 points on volume of 778.6 million shares worth 8.9 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index put on 79.074 points or 2.76 percent to 2,942.143 points.
Yunnan Baoshan Cement was the star on talk of institutional interest, surging 0.71 yuan or 10.07 percent to 7.76 yuan on volume of 2.9 million shares.
